To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single systemic injection of the long-lasting kappa opioid receptor (kOR) antagonist norbinaltrophimine (nor-BNI) given 2 or 3 days after exposure to footshock attenuates the expression and/or the development of fear and anxiety.
a post-shock injection of the KOP antagonist norBNI (30 mg/kg) attenuated the expression of shock-induced fear but did not attenuate generalized fear, and that the same dose had anxiolytical effects.
systemic injection of a KOR antagonist attenuates the expression and enhances the recovery from the expression of fear but not anxiety produced by exposure to an acute stressor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the KOR in the expression of negative emotions and suggests that the KOR is involved in the modulation of the anxiety component of a negative emotional state.
the role of the KOR in mediating the expression of negative emotions in response to stressors.
understanding the neurobiological mechanisms underlying stress-induced emotional states.

norBNI had a significant anxiolytic but not a significant anti-fear effect in rats.
norBNI is a mixed anxiolytic and anxiogenic compound.
the KOR antagonist has mixed effect on fear but anxiolytic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the KOR system may be involved in the expression of anxiety-like behaviors in the absence of fear and in the expression of fear in the presence of anxiogenic stimuli.
the KOR antagonist, norBNI, has anxiolytic but not anxiogenic effects in rats.
the KOR system plays a role in the expression of fear but not generalized fear.

the KOR antagonist has the potential to be a useful tool in treating the anxiety associated with post-traumatic stress disorder.
